QUESTION 001Interview essentials
# q1

What are virtual threads in Java 21?

Say this in the interview

Virtual threads are lightweight threads managed by the JVM. They let us use a thread-per-request style for high-concurrency, blocking I/O workloads without allocating one OS thread per request. They improve throughput, not CPU execution speed.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Use virtual threads for blocking network or database calls. Limit access to scarce resources such as database connections separately. In Java 21, blocking inside synchronized blocks can pin a carrier thread; profile pinning and avoid holding monitors during long I/O. Do not pool virtual threads.

Example / implementation sketch
try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
    var result = executor.submit(() -> callRemoteService());
    System.out.println(result.get());
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How would you limit downstream concurrency?
  • When can virtual threads be pinned?

QUESTION 002Interview essentials
# q2

How does HashMap work internally?

Say this in the interview

HashMap hashes a key to choose a bucket and uses equals to find the matching key within it. Collisions share a bucket; sufficiently large collision chains can become balanced trees. Average get and put are O(1), assuming well-distributed hashes.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Keys must have consistent equals and hashCode implementations. Mutable keys can become unreachable after insertion. HashMap is not thread-safe; use ConcurrentHashMap for concurrent access. Resizing redistributes buckets when the load threshold is exceeded.

Example / implementation sketch
Map<String, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
counts.merge("payment", 1, Integer::sum);

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why must equal objects have equal hash codes?
  • When would you use ConcurrentHashMap?

QUESTION 003Interview essentials
# q3

What is the difference between map and filter in Java streams?

Say this in the interview

filter selects elements using a boolean predicate and keeps their type. map transforms each element into another value, possibly with a different type. Use filter to keep eligible employees and map to extract their salaries.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Streams are lazy until a terminal operation runs. Avoid side effects in intermediate operations. Use flatMap when one input produces multiple elements that should be flattened.

Example / implementation sketch
var salaries = employees.stream()
    .filter(e -> e.getSalary() > 50000)
    .map(Employee::getSalary)
    .toList();

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • When would you use flatMap?
  • What makes a stream lazy?

QUESTION 004Interview essentials
# q4

What are records and sealed classes?

Say this in the interview

Records are concise data carriers with generated accessors, equals, hashCode and toString. Sealed classes restrict which types can extend or implement them. Together they model explicit domain alternatives with less boilerplate.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Records are shallowly immutable: referenced collections may still be mutable. Sealed hierarchies combine well with exhaustive pattern-matching switches in Java 21. Use defensive copies for collection components.

Example / implementation sketch
sealed interface Result permits Success, Failure {}
record Success(String value) implements Result {}
record Failure(String message) implements Result {}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Are records deeply immutable?
  • How does an exhaustive switch help?

QUESTION 005Interview essentials
# q5

What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?

Say this in the interview

Checked exceptions must be caught or declared and represent failures callers are expected to consider. Unchecked exceptions extend RuntimeException and need no declaration. Choose based on whether recovery is part of the caller’s contract.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Avoid catching Exception everywhere or swallowing the cause. Translate infrastructure failures at a clear boundary, preserve the cause, and return an appropriate API error without exposing internal details.

Example / implementation sketch
try {
    repository.save(payment);
} catch (SQLException ex) {
    throw new PaymentStorageException("Save failed", ex);
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Should you retry every exception?
  • How do you preserve the root cause?

QUESTION 006Interview essentials
# q6

What is the difference between synchronized and volatile?

Say this in the interview

synchronized provides mutual exclusion and visibility for code protected by the same monitor. volatile provides visibility and ordering for reads and writes of a variable, but does not make compound operations like count++ atomic.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Use AtomicInteger for atomic increments, or a lock when multiple values must change consistently. Visibility alone cannot protect an invariant that spans several operations.

Example / implementation sketch
private final AtomicInteger count = new AtomicInteger();
public int increment() { return count.incrementAndGet(); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Is volatile count++ atomic?
  • What is a happens-before relationship?

QUESTION 007Interview essentials
# q36

What is the Java Memory Model and a happens-before relationship?

Say this in the interview

The Java Memory Model defines how threads observe shared memory. A happens-before relationship guarantees that earlier writes are visible to a later operation. Examples include unlocking and then locking the same monitor, or writing and then reading the same volatile variable.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Without appropriate synchronization, a program can have data races and observe stale values or unexpected ordering. Thread.start makes prior actions visible to the started thread; a successful join makes the completed thread’s actions visible to its caller. Happens-before is a visibility and ordering guarantee, not a promise about elapsed time.

Example / implementation sketch
private int value;
private volatile boolean ready;

void publish() { value = 42; ready = true; }
void consume() {
    if (ready) System.out.println(value); // sees 42 after publication
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why is volatile insufficient for count++?
  • How does safe publication work?

QUESTION 008Interview essentials
# q37

What is the difference between == and equals in Java?

Say this in the interview

For primitives, == compares values. For object references, == checks whether both references point to the same object. equals checks logical equality as defined by the class; Object’s default implementation uses reference identity. Classes that override equals must also provide a consistent hashCode.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

String overrides equals to compare contents. String interning can make reference comparisons appear to work for literals, but == is not a reliable content comparison. Use Objects.equals when either reference may be null. For arrays, use Arrays.equals or Arrays.deepEquals as appropriate.

Example / implementation sketch
String first = new String("Java");
String second = new String("Java");
System.out.println(first == second);      // false
System.out.println(first.equals(second)); // true

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why must equals and hashCode agree?
  • How do you compare arrays by content?

QUESTION 009Interview essentials
# q38

What is Optional and when should you use it?

Say this in the interview

Optional represents a value that may be absent and is most useful as a return type. Use map, flatMap and orElseGet to handle absence explicitly. Avoid calling get without checking and avoid returning null instead of Optional.empty.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

orElse evaluates its fallback eagerly, while orElseGet calls a supplier only when the Optional is empty. Optional does not replace validation or all nullable fields. Collection-returning APIs normally return an empty collection rather than Optional<List<T>>.

Example / implementation sketch
String name = repository.findById(id) // Optional<Customer>
    .map(Customer::getName)
    .orElseGet(() -> loadDefaultName());

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What is the difference between orElse and orElseGet?
  • When do you need Optional.flatMap?

QUESTION 010Interview essentials
# q39

How is CompletableFuture different from Future?

Say this in the interview

Future represents a pending result and usually requires blocking with get to retrieve it. CompletableFuture also supports composing stages, combining independent results and handling failures. Use an appropriate executor for blocking work instead of unintentionally exhausting the shared common pool.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Use thenApply for a synchronous transformation and thenCompose when the next operation returns another stage. Async methods schedule work through an executor; non-async callbacks may run on the completing thread. Timeouts do not necessarily cancel the underlying operation, so configure downstream timeouts too.

Example / implementation sketch
CompletableFuture<Summary> summary =
    loadCustomerAsync(id)
        .thenCombine(loadOrdersAsync(id), Summary::new)
        .orTimeout(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS);

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • When should you use thenCompose instead of thenApply?
  • Does a timeout stop the underlying task?

QUESTION 011Interview essentials
# q71

How does pattern matching for switch work in Java 21?

Say this in the interview

Pattern matching lets a switch select a branch based on a value’s type and bind a variable for that branch. Java 21 also supports guards and explicit null cases. With sealed types, an exhaustive switch helps the compiler detect missing alternatives.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Put more specific patterns before broader ones to avoid dominated cases. Use a when guard for extra conditions. Null must be handled explicitly when allowed; a default branch alone does not automatically handle null. Exhaustiveness is checked against the selector type and covered patterns.

Example / implementation sketch
String describe(Object value) {
    return switch (value) {
        case null -> "missing";
        case Integer n when n > 0 -> "positive integer";
        case String s -> "text: " + s;
        default -> "other";
    };
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What is a dominated case?
  • Does default automatically match null?

QUESTION 012Interview essentials
# q72

How do you create an immutable class in Java?

Say this in the interview

Keep state private, prevent uncontrolled subclassing, initialize it in the constructor and expose no mutators. Defensively copy mutable inputs and outputs, including nested state when needed. final fields prevent reassignment but do not make the referenced objects immutable.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Records reduce boilerplate but are only shallowly immutable. List.copyOf prevents structural changes through the copied list; mutable elements still need their own protection. Immutability simplifies sharing across threads, but safely publishing the object and avoiding constructor escape still matter.

Example / implementation sketch
public record Team(List<String> members) {
    public Team {
        members = List.copyOf(members);
    }
}
// String elements are immutable; the list cannot be structurally changed.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why is final List insufficient?
  • What makes a record only shallowly immutable?

QUESTION 013Interview essentials
# q73

What is the difference between a memory leak and high garbage collection pressure?

Say this in the interview

A memory leak retains objects that are no longer useful, so the live heap tends to grow. High allocation pressure creates many temporary objects and frequent garbage collection even when they are reclaimed. Compare allocation rate, post-GC heap usage and retention paths before choosing a fix.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Use GC logs and Java Flight Recorder to identify allocation hotspots, then inspect heap dumps when retained growth suggests a leak. Unbounded caches, listeners and ThreadLocal values are common retention sources. A large heap or frequent GC alone does not prove a leak.

Example / implementation sketch
# Diagnostic examples; verify tools and operational impact first.
jcmd <pid> GC.heap_info
jcmd <pid> JFR.start name=diagnostic settings=profile duration=60s filename=diagnostic.jfr

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What would steadily rising post-GC heap usage suggest?
  • How can a ThreadLocal retain objects?

QUESTION 014Interview essentials
# q107

What is the difference between ArrayList and LinkedList?

Say this in the interview

ArrayList stores elements in a resizable array and offers constant-time indexed access. LinkedList uses linked nodes and requires traversal for indexing. ArrayList is usually the better default because of locality and lower allocation overhead.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

LinkedList insertion is constant-time only once the insertion position is already known. Searching for that position can dominate the operation; benchmark the actual access pattern.

Example / implementation sketch
List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why can LinkedList insertion still be O(n)?
  • How does memory locality affect performance?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 015Interview essentials
# q108

How does ConcurrentHashMap support concurrent access?

Say this in the interview

ConcurrentHashMap supports concurrent retrieval and updates without locking the entire map for every operation. Use atomic methods such as computeIfAbsent or merge for compound operations rather than separate check-then-put steps.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

It rejects null keys and values. Iteration is weakly consistent, and a thread-safe map does not automatically make mutable values stored inside it thread-safe.

Example / implementation sketch
counts.merge(key, 1, Integer::sum);

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why is containsKey followed by put unsafe?
  • Can a mutable map value still have data races?

QUESTION 016Interview essentials
# q109

What is the difference between Comparable and Comparator?

Say this in the interview

Comparable defines a type’s natural ordering through compareTo. Comparator defines an external ordering and allows several sort orders for the same type. Prefer composable comparators when ordering depends on the use case.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Sorted sets and maps use comparison equality to identify equivalent keys. An ordering inconsistent with equals can therefore produce surprising membership behavior.

Example / implementation sketch
employees.sort(Comparator.comparing(Employee::getName).thenComparing(Employee::getId));

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What happens when compare returns zero?
  • How would you handle null sort keys?

QUESTION 017Interview essentials
# q110

What is type erasure in Java generics?

Say this in the interview

Java checks most generic type constraints at compile time and erases type parameters to their bounds in generated code. Consequently, List<String> and List<Integer> do not have separate runtime classes.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Erasure limits operations such as new T() and instanceof List<String>. Avoid raw types; unchecked casts can postpone a type error until a value is retrieved.

Example / implementation sketch
List<String> values = new ArrayList<>(); // retain compile-time type safety

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why can you not create new T()?
  • What risks do raw types introduce?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 018Interview essentials
# q111

What does PECS mean for generic wildcards?

Say this in the interview

PECS means producer extends, consumer super. Use ? extends T when reading T values from a source and ? super T when writing T values to a destination. Use a concrete type when both operations need the same precise type.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

An extends wildcard does not generally allow inserting arbitrary T values because its actual subtype is unknown. A super wildcard reads as Object unless narrowed safely.

Example / implementation sketch
static <T> void copy(List<? extends T> src, List<? super T> dst) { dst.addAll(src); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why can you not add a Number to List<? extends Number>?
  • When is a wildcard unnecessary?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 019Interview essentials
# q112

What is the difference between an interface default method and a static method?

Say this in the interview

A default method is an inherited instance implementation that implementing classes can override. An interface static method belongs to the interface itself and is called using the interface name; it is not inherited as an instance method.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Conflicting defaults from unrelated interfaces require an explicit resolution. Default methods help evolve interfaces, but shared mutable state still does not belong in interface fields.

Example / implementation sketch
interface Named { default String label() { return "name"; } static boolean valid(String s) { return s != null; } }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do you resolve two conflicting default methods?
  • Can an interface static method be overridden?

QUESTION 020Interview essentials
# q113

How do fail-fast and weakly consistent iterators differ?

Say this in the interview

Fail-fast iterators may detect structural modification and throw ConcurrentModificationException. Weakly consistent iterators, such as those of ConcurrentHashMap, tolerate concurrent changes and may reflect some updates without providing a single fixed snapshot.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Fail-fast detection is best effort and is not a concurrency guarantee. A CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator instead uses a snapshot, with copying costs paid during updates.

Example / implementation sketch
for (var entry : concurrentMap.entrySet()) { inspect(entry); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Is ConcurrentModificationException guaranteed?
  • When would CopyOnWriteArrayList be suitable?

QUESTION 021Interview essentials
# q114

How do intermediate and terminal stream operations differ?

Say this in the interview

Intermediate operations build a lazy pipeline and usually return another stream. A terminal operation triggers processing and produces a result or side effect. A stream is single-use and cannot be reused after a terminal operation.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Short-circuiting terminals can avoid processing every element. Avoid relying on side effects inside intermediate operations because optimization and traversal behavior can affect their execution.

Example / implementation sketch
long count = values.stream().filter(v -> v > 0).count();

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Which operations short-circuit?
  • Why should intermediate operations avoid side effects?

QUESTION 022Interview essentials
# q115

When should you avoid parallel streams?

Say this in the interview

Avoid parallel streams when work blocks heavily, data is small, ordering costs dominate or operations share mutable state. They can help CPU-intensive work on suitable data, but only when splitting and combining costs are justified.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Parallel execution commonly uses the shared common pool, so blocking work can interfere with other tasks. Measure throughput and latency under a representative workload.

Example / implementation sketch
long total = values.parallelStream().mapToLong(this::cpuWork).sum();

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why can parallel execution be slower?
  • What makes a reduction safe to parallelize?

QUESTION 023Interview essentials
# q116

What is the difference between reduce and collect?

Say this in the interview

reduce combines values using an associative operation, ideally without mutable shared state. collect supports mutable accumulation through a supplier, accumulator and combiner, making it suitable for building collections or grouped results.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Parallel correctness depends on compatible identity and combination rules. Do not mutate one shared list from a reduce accumulator; use collectors or an appropriate collection supplier.

Example / implementation sketch
Map<String, Long> counts = events.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Event::type, Collectors.counting()));

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why must a parallel reduction be associative?
  • Why is mutating a shared identity unsafe?

QUESTION 024Interview essentials
# q117

How does try-with-resources work?

Say this in the interview

Try-with-resources automatically closes AutoCloseable resources when the block finishes, including exceptional paths. Multiple resources close in reverse declaration order. It reduces leaks and preserves the main exception when closing also fails.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Closing failures can appear as suppressed exceptions. Ownership still matters: do not close a resource that a caller or framework expects to keep using.

Example / implementation sketch
try (InputStream in = Files.newInputStream(path)) { return in.readAllBytes(); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What are suppressed exceptions?
  • In what order are multiple resources closed?

QUESTION 025Interview essentials
# q118

How does Java interruption work?

Say this in the interview

Interruption is a cooperative cancellation signal, not a forced thread kill. Blocking methods may throw InterruptedException; code should stop or propagate appropriately. If you cannot propagate the exception, normally restore the interrupt flag before returning.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Thread.interrupted reads and clears the current thread’s flag, while isInterrupted does not clear it. Avoid swallowing interruption and continuing indefinitely.

Example / implementation sketch
catch (InterruptedException ex) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); return; }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why restore the interrupt flag?
  • Does interrupt immediately stop CPU-bound code?

QUESTION 026Interview essentials
# q119

What is ThreadLocal and what are its risks?

Say this in the interview

ThreadLocal stores a separate value for each thread. It can hold thread-bound context, but values must be removed when their scope ends, especially with pooled threads. Otherwise data can leak across tasks or remain retained.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Virtual threads can make per-thread heavyweight objects expensive at high concurrency. ThreadLocal context does not automatically propagate across arbitrary asynchronous boundaries.

Example / implementation sketch
try { context.set(requestId); process(); } finally { context.remove(); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why do pooled threads need cleanup?
  • Does ThreadLocal automatically follow CompletableFuture stages?

QUESTION 027Interview essentials
# q120

How should you implement equals and hashCode for a value object?

Say this in the interview

Base both methods on the same stable logical fields. equals must be reflexive, symmetric, transitive and consistent, and return false for null. Equal objects must have equal hash codes; unequal objects may still share a hash code.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Avoid mutable fields in hash keys. Inheritance can complicate symmetry; records or carefully designed final value classes can simplify the contract.

Example / implementation sketch
record AccountKey(String tenantId, String accountId) {}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why does mutating a key break lookup?
  • Must unequal objects have different hash codes?

QUESTION 028Interview essentials
# q121

Why use BigDecimal for monetary calculations?

Say this in the interview

BigDecimal represents decimal values with explicit precision and scale, avoiding many binary floating-point surprises. Construct it from decimal strings or suitable factory methods, and choose rounding rules explicitly for financial operations.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

equals includes scale, while compareTo compares numerical value. Division can require an explicit rounding rule when the decimal result does not terminate.

Example / implementation sketch
BigDecimal amount = new BigDecimal("10.25"); BigDecimal half = amount.divide(BigDecimal.valueOf(2), 2, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN);

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do equals and compareTo differ for BigDecimal?
  • Why avoid new BigDecimal(0.1)?

QUESTION 029Interview essentials
# q122

What is a Java functional interface?

Say this in the interview

A functional interface has one abstract method, allowing lambdas and method references to supply its behavior. Default and static methods do not count toward that abstract-method total. Common examples include Predicate, Function, Consumer and Supplier.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

The @FunctionalInterface annotation asks the compiler to verify the contract. Captured local variables must be final or effectively final; mutable referenced objects can still create concurrency risks.

Example / implementation sketch
Predicate<String> nonBlank = s -> s != null && !s.isBlank();

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do Function and Consumer differ?
  • What does effectively final mean?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 030Interview essentials
# q123

How do platform threads and virtual threads differ operationally?

Say this in the interview

Platform threads typically map to operating-system threads; virtual threads are scheduled by the JVM over carrier threads. Virtual threads support large numbers of blocking tasks, but they do not increase CPU capacity or remove downstream resource limits.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

In Java 21, some blocking patterns can pin carrier threads. Observe pinning, database limits and allocation pressure before assuming more concurrent tasks mean more throughput.

Example / implementation sketch
try (var executor = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) { executor.submit(this::blockingIo); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What workload benefits most?
  • Why can too many concurrent database calls still hurt?

QUESTION 031Interview essentials
# q7

How does Spring Boot auto-configuration work?

Say this in the interview

Spring Boot conditionally registers configuration based on the classpath, properties and existing beans. It supplies sensible defaults and usually backs off when you provide your own bean. @SpringBootApplication enables auto-configuration, component scanning and configuration.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Use the condition evaluation report to understand why a configuration matched. Auto-configuration imports are declared through AutoConfiguration.imports. Narrow exclusions instead of disabling auto-configuration broadly.

Example / implementation sketch
@SpringBootApplication
public class PaymentsApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(PaymentsApplication.class, args);
    }
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do you debug an unexpected bean?
  • When does auto-configuration back off?

QUESTION 032Interview essentials
# q8

How does @Transactional work and what are its pitfalls?

Say this in the interview

Spring usually applies @Transactional through a proxy that opens or joins a transaction around a method. By default, RuntimeException and Error trigger rollback. Self-invocation bypasses proxy advice, and checked exceptions need an explicit rollback rule when rollback is required.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Keep transaction boundaries in the service layer. Avoid holding a database transaction open across slow remote calls. Propagation defines whether to join or create a transaction; isolation governs visibility of concurrent changes.

Example / implementation sketch
@Transactional(rollbackFor = IOException.class)
public void transfer(Transfer request) throws IOException {
    debit(request);
    credit(request);
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why does self-invocation bypass the transaction?
  • What does REQUIRES_NEW do?

QUESTION 033Interview essentials
# q9

How do you resolve multiple beans of the same type?

Say this in the interview

Use @Qualifier when the injection point needs a specific bean, or @Primary for the default choice. Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit. For multiple data sources, qualify each DataSource, EntityManagerFactory and transaction manager consistently.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Check component scanning and auto-configuration before adding a qualifier: an unintended duplicate may be the actual issue. For JPA, associate repository packages with the intended entity manager and transaction manager.

Example / implementation sketch
public PaymentService(@Qualifier("primaryClient") PaymentClient client) {
    this.client = client;
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • When is @Primary inappropriate?
  • How do you configure two data sources?

QUESTION 034Interview essentials
# q10

WebClient versus RestClient: which should I use?

Say this in the interview

RestClient provides a synchronous fluent HTTP client. WebClient provides a reactive, non-blocking API and supports streaming. Choose based on the application’s execution model; calling block on WebClient makes that call synchronous.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Set connection and response timeouts, handle errors explicitly, and bound retries. In a reactive pipeline, avoid blocking operations on event-loop threads. SOAP additionally needs XML envelopes, namespaces and a SOAP-aware client such as Spring Web Services WebServiceTemplate.

Example / implementation sketch
var response = restClient.get()
    .uri("/payments/{id}", id)
    .retrieve()
    .body(Payment.class);

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do you set timeouts?
  • What would you use for SOAP?

QUESTION 035Interview essentials
# q40

What are Spring bean scopes, and are singleton beans thread-safe?

Say this in the interview

Singleton is the default scope: one bean instance per bean definition per application context. Prototype creates a new instance each time the container is asked for that bean. Singleton scope does not make a bean thread-safe; prefer stateless services or synchronize mutable shared state.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Web-aware contexts also support request and session scopes. Injecting a prototype into a singleton normally resolves it once when the singleton is created. Use ObjectProvider or a scoped proxy when a fresh or request-scoped instance is needed later. Do not store request-specific data in singleton fields.

Example / implementation sketch
@Service
class PaymentService {
    // Keep per-request data in method arguments and local variables.
    Receipt pay(Payment request) { return process(request); }
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What happens when you inject a prototype into a singleton?
  • Where should request-specific state live?

QUESTION 036Interview essentials
# q41

How do you implement global exception handling in a REST API?

Say this in the interview

Use @RestControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler to translate exceptions into consistent HTTP responses. Return suitable status codes and a stable error body, such as ProblemDetail. Log diagnostic details with a correlation ID while keeping stack traces and sensitive internal details out of responses.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Separate client validation failures from missing resources, conflicts and unexpected server errors. Spring MVC controller advice does not automatically handle every security-filter failure; configure the authentication entry point and access-denied handler for those boundaries. Validate request bodies with Bean Validation where appropriate.

Example / implementation sketch
@RestControllerAdvice
class ApiErrors {
    @ExceptionHandler(PaymentNotFoundException.class)
    ProblemDetail notFound(PaymentNotFoundException ex) {
        return ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(
            HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Payment not found");
    }
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Which failures should return 400, 404 or 409?
  • Does controller advice handle security-filter exceptions?

QUESTION 037Interview essentials
# q42

What is the N+1 query problem in JPA and how do you fix it?

Say this in the interview

N+1 happens when one query loads parent records and accessing a relationship triggers additional queries for each parent. Detect it through SQL logs or tracing. Fix it with a query-specific fetch join, entity graph, DTO projection or batching, based on the data the endpoint actually needs.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Making every relationship eager can create more unnecessary queries or oversized results. Collection fetch joins can complicate pagination and multiply rows; consider paging IDs first and fetching the required data separately. Verify generated SQL and query counts rather than assuming an annotation solved the issue.

Example / implementation sketch
@EntityGraph(attributePaths = "customer")
@Query("select p from Payment p where p.status = :status")
List<Payment> findWithCustomer(@Param("status") Status status);

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why is eager loading not a universal fix?
  • What happens when you paginate a collection fetch join?

QUESTION 038Interview essentials
# q74

What are the differences between @Component, @Service and @Repository?

Say this in the interview

All three can register component-scanned Spring beans. @Service expresses business-service intent; @Repository marks persistence components and can participate in exception translation when the relevant infrastructure is enabled. @Component is the general-purpose stereotype. Choose the annotation that describes the class’s responsibility.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

@Service does not automatically create a transaction, and @Repository is not a substitute for configuring persistence. Keep controllers focused on HTTP concerns, services on use cases, and repositories on data access. Constructor injection makes those dependencies clear.

Example / implementation sketch
@Service
class PaymentService {
    private final PaymentRepository repository;
    PaymentService(PaymentRepository repository) {
        this.repository = repository;
    }
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Does @Service automatically enable transactions?
  • What does persistence exception translation do?

QUESTION 039Interview essentials
# q75

How do you validate incoming requests in Spring Boot?

Say this in the interview

Use Bean Validation constraints on request DTOs and @Valid at the controller boundary. Return clear client errors for invalid input and validate business invariants in the service layer as well. Database constraints provide an additional guarantee against invalid or conflicting concurrent writes.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Nested objects need cascading validation, and method-validation setup depends on the framework version and entry point. Validation annotations do not replace authorization or concurrency-safe checks. Keep validation errors consistent through your global exception handling.

Example / implementation sketch
record TransferRequest(
    @NotBlank String accountId,
    @NotNull @DecimalMin("0.01") BigDecimal amount) {}

@PostMapping("/transfers")
Receipt transfer(@Valid @RequestBody TransferRequest request) {
    return service.transfer(request);
}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How is input validation different from a business invariant?
  • Why are database constraints still necessary?

QUESTION 040Interview essentials
# q76

How does Spring Boot externalized configuration work?

Say this in the interview

Spring Boot combines configuration from sources such as properties files, environment variables and command-line arguments according to precedence rules. Use @ConfigurationProperties for grouped, typed settings and validate required values. Keep environment-specific values outside the application image and secrets in an appropriate secret store.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Profiles select configuration for different environments; they are not an access-control boundary. Higher-priority sources can override file values, so inspect effective configuration carefully without logging secrets. Prefer explicit typed properties over scattered @Value expressions for related settings.

Example / implementation sketch
@Validated
@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "payments.client")
public record ClientProperties(
    @NotNull Duration timeout,
    @NotNull URI baseUrl) {}
// Register via @ConfigurationPropertiesScan or @EnableConfigurationProperties.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do you debug an unexpected property override?
  • Why use @ConfigurationProperties instead of many @Value fields?

QUESTION 041Interview essentials
# q124

How do constructor injection and field injection differ?

Say this in the interview

Constructor injection makes required dependencies explicit and allows final fields. It makes ordinary unit tests easier and exposes excessive dependencies. Field injection hides construction requirements and usually requires reflection or a framework to initialize the object.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

A single constructor can generally be used without @Autowired. Constructor cycles often reveal misplaced responsibilities and should prompt a design review.

Example / implementation sketch
PaymentService(PaymentRepository repository) { this.repository = repository; }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why are final dependency fields useful?
  • What can a constructor cycle indicate?

QUESTION 042Interview essentials
# q125

What is the difference between @Controller and @RestController?

Say this in the interview

@Controller participates in MVC handling and commonly returns view names. @RestController combines @Controller with @ResponseBody so handler return values are written to the response body through message converters. It does not automatically define status codes or error semantics.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

A String return value has different meaning depending on response-body handling. Use ResponseEntity when explicit headers, status and body control are helpful.

Example / implementation sketch
@GetMapping("/health-label") String label() { return "ready"; } // body under @RestController

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • When would you use ResponseEntity?
  • What does a String return mean in a view controller?

QUESTION 043Interview essentials
# q126

How does Spring MVC differ from Spring WebFlux?

Say this in the interview

Spring MVC is built around the servlet stack, while WebFlux supports a reactive execution model. Choose based on the whole request path and dependencies. Returning Mono does not make a blocking database driver non-blocking.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

In reactive flows, blocking the event loop can harm many requests. MVC with appropriate concurrency may be simpler when most dependencies are blocking.

Example / implementation sketch
Mono<Payment> payment = reactiveClient.getPayment(id); // keep the full chain non-blocking

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • When is MVC the simpler choice?
  • Why is blocking on an event loop harmful?

QUESTION 044Interview essentials
# q127

How does @Async work in Spring?

Say this in the interview

@Async usually submits an intercepted method invocation to an executor through a Spring proxy. Calling that method directly within the same object bypasses normal proxy advice. Configure an appropriate executor and make error handling explicit.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Async execution does not automatically propagate thread-bound transaction or logging context. A new asynchronous task needs its own suitable transaction boundary when accessing transactional resources.

Example / implementation sketch
@Async("paymentExecutor") CompletableFuture<Receipt> processAsync(Payment p) { return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(process(p)); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What happens with self-invocation?
  • Does the caller’s transaction follow the async task?

QUESTION 045Interview essentials
# q128

What are transaction propagation modes?

Say this in the interview

Propagation defines how a transactional method interacts with an existing transaction. REQUIRED normally joins or creates one; REQUIRES_NEW starts an independent transaction and suspends the outer one. Choose according to the desired commit and rollback boundaries.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Independent transactions can consume additional connections and commit even if the outer transaction later rolls back. NESTED behavior depends on savepoint and transaction-manager support.

Example / implementation sketch
@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW) void recordAudit(Audit a) { repository.save(a); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Can an inner commit survive an outer rollback?
  • How can REQUIRES_NEW exhaust a connection pool?

QUESTION 046Interview essentials
# q129

What do transaction isolation levels control?

Say this in the interview

Isolation levels define which effects of concurrent transactions a transaction may observe. They address phenomena such as dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and serialization anomalies. Actual behavior depends on the database, so choose and test against required invariants.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Higher isolation can increase coordination, conflicts or retries. An isolation label alone is not a substitute for a concurrency-safe balance update or unique constraint.

Example / implementation sketch
@Transactional(isolation = Isolation.SERIALIZABLE) void reserve(ResourceId id) { reserveSafely(id); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why might serializable transactions need retries?
  • Is isolation behavior identical across databases?

QUESTION 047Interview essentials
# q130

How do you configure more than one transaction manager?

Say this in the interview

Define transaction managers for the appropriate persistence resources and select one explicitly with @Transactional when needed. Associate each repository group with its intended entity manager and transaction manager. A local transaction manager normally coordinates its own resource.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Two local transaction managers do not automatically provide an atomic distributed transaction. Cross-database workflows need an explicit consistency and recovery strategy.

Example / implementation sketch
@Transactional(transactionManager = "ledgerTransactionManager") void postEntry(Entry entry) { ledger.save(entry); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Does this make two databases atomic?
  • What happens if the wrong repository group is wired?

QUESTION 048Interview essentials
# q131

What are JPA entity lifecycle states?

Say this in the interview

JPA entities can be new, managed, detached or removed. Managed entities belong to a persistence context and can be tracked for changes. Detached entities no longer receive that tracking; merging copies state into a managed instance.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

merge returns the managed instance and does not simply reattach the original object. Lazy access outside the required context can fail, so shape queries and DTOs deliberately.

Example / implementation sketch
Payment managed = entityManager.merge(detachedPayment);

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Does merge make the original instance managed?
  • Why can lazy loading fail after the transaction ends?

QUESTION 049Interview essentials
# q132

What is dirty checking in JPA?

Say this in the interview

Dirty checking detects changes to managed entities and translates them into database updates during flushing. An explicit repository save is not always required for every managed-field change inside a transaction. Flush timing and transaction commit are distinct.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Flushing can happen before commit, including before certain queries. Constraint errors may therefore appear earlier than expected, while detached entity changes are not automatically tracked.

Example / implementation sketch
@Transactional void rename(Long id, String name) { repository.findById(id).orElseThrow().setName(name); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Is flush the same as commit?
  • Are detached objects dirty-checked?

QUESTION 050Interview essentials
# q133

How do you choose DTOs instead of exposing JPA entities?

Say this in the interview

DTOs define the API’s intended data independently of persistence structure. They reduce accidental exposure, avoid serialization surprises from lazy relationships and allow explicit validation. Map only the fields the operation needs.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Exposing entities can couple API evolution to database changes and enable unwanted writes through request binding. Projections can avoid loading unnecessary data for read-heavy endpoints.

Example / implementation sketch
record PaymentResponse(String id, String status) {}

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do DTOs reduce over-posting risks?
  • When is a database projection useful?

QUESTION 051Interview essentials
# q134

How does Spring caching work and what are common pitfalls?

Say this in the interview

Spring caching typically applies cache operations through proxies around annotated methods. @Cacheable can reuse a stored result; @CacheEvict removes entries. Choose stable keys and a freshness policy, and remember that self-invocation usually bypasses proxy advice.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Caching does not automatically synchronize all concurrent misses or make data globally consistent. Consider distributed deployment, cache invalidation and serialization when choosing a cache implementation.

Example / implementation sketch
@Cacheable(cacheNames = "products", key = "#id") Product findProduct(String id) { return repository.load(id); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How does self-invocation affect caching?
  • How would you prevent stale cached data?

QUESTION 052Interview essentials
# q135

How do you schedule background work in Spring?

Say this in the interview

Enable scheduling and use @Scheduled for suitable periodic tasks. Define execution duration, overlap and error handling. A scheduled method may run in every application replica, so use coordination or an external scheduler when only one execution should own a job.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Fixed delay waits after completion; fixed rate targets a regular cadence. Neither provides a durable distributed job history or exactly-once execution by itself.

Example / implementation sketch
@Scheduled(fixedDelayString = "PT1M") void reconcile() { reconciliation.runBatch(); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do fixed rate and fixed delay differ?
  • What changes when the service has five replicas?

QUESTION 053Interview essentials
# q136

What is the purpose of Spring Boot Actuator?

Say this in the interview

Actuator exposes operational features such as health information and metrics. Enable and expose only the endpoints needed by operators, secure sensitive endpoints and integrate useful signals with monitoring. Endpoint exposure and endpoint access control are separate configuration concerns.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Health details can reveal infrastructure information. Keep liveness focused on process health and design readiness to reflect whether the instance should receive traffic.

Example / implementation sketch
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info,prometheus

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why should every actuator endpoint not be publicly exposed?
  • How do readiness and liveness groups differ?

QUESTION 054Interview essentials
# q137

How do Spring Security filters relate to controllers?

Say this in the interview

Spring Security processes requests through a filter chain before controller handling. Authentication and authorization failures can be handled there, so MVC controller advice is not the universal error boundary. Configure entry points and access-denied handling consistently.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Multiple security chains need explicit request matching and ordering. A valid identity still requires operation and resource-level authorization.

Example / implementation sketch
// Configure SecurityFilterChain request matchers and access rules; keep sensitive authorization server-side.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why might a request never reach the controller?
  • How do 401 and 403 differ?

QUESTION 055Interview essentials
# q138

How should you handle pagination for large database result sets?

Say this in the interview

Bound page size and select a stable ordering. Offset pagination is simple but can become expensive and unstable as data changes. Keyset pagination uses the last seen ordering key and often works better for large sequential traversals.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

A unique tie-breaker prevents ambiguous ordering. Count queries and collection fetch joins can be costly; return a slice or cursor when an exact total is unnecessary.

Example / implementation sketch
SELECT * FROM payment WHERE id > :lastId ORDER BY id LIMIT :pageSize;

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why does a cursor need stable ordering?
  • When is an exact total count unnecessary?

QUESTION 056Interview essentials
# q139

How do you safely upgrade a major Spring Boot version?

Say this in the interview

Review supported Java, Gradle and dependency versions, then update deprecated APIs, configuration and framework integrations. Upgrade in a controlled branch and validate startup plus critical application behavior, including persistence, security and messaging.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

A successful compile does not prove runtime compatibility. Pay attention to managed dependency overrides, namespace changes and test infrastructure; deploy gradually with observable rollback criteria.

Example / implementation sketch
// Baseline tests → align BOM/toolchain → update APIs → integration checks → staged rollout.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Which runtime areas deserve extra testing?
  • Why can overriding managed versions break an upgrade?

QUESTION 057Interview essentials
# q140

When would you use Spring Web Services for SOAP integration?

Say this in the interview

Use a SOAP-aware client such as WebServiceTemplate when you need SOAP envelopes, XML marshalling, faults or protocol-specific features. A generic HTTP client can send XML but leaves more SOAP behavior to your own implementation.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Bind the expected schemas and namespaces, configure transport timeouts and TLS, and handle SOAP faults separately from HTTP transport errors. Avoid logging sensitive XML payloads indiscriminately.

Example / implementation sketch
Object response = webServiceTemplate.marshalSendAndReceive(request);

  • How does a SOAP fault differ from an HTTP connection failure?

QUESTION 058Interview essentials
# q11

How do you make a payment API idempotent?

Say this in the interview

Require an idempotency key and store it with the request fingerprint and outcome. Atomically ensure only one operation owns that key; repeated identical requests receive the original result. Reject key reuse with a different payload.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

A read-then-insert check races under concurrency. Use a unique constraint or conditional write, track in-progress states, and define retention. Coordinate external side effects with provider idempotency and an outbox or recoverable workflow.

Example / implementation sketch
INSERT INTO idempotency_request (key, request_hash, status)
VALUES (:key, :hash, 'PROCESSING');
-- unique constraint on key; resolve conflicts safely

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What happens if the server crashes after charging?
  • How long do you retain keys?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 059Interview essentials
# q12

What is a circuit breaker and how is it different from retry?

Say this in the interview

A retry repeats a transient failed call. A circuit breaker stops calls to a failing dependency once a threshold is reached, then probes recovery. Combine them with timeouts, bounded attempts and backoff to prevent cascading failures.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Retries can amplify outages and duplicate side effects. Retry only appropriate failures and idempotent operations, with exponential backoff and jitter. A bulkhead separately limits concurrency or resources for a dependency.

Example / implementation sketch
// Example Resilience4j annotation
@CircuitBreaker(name = "payments", fallbackMethod = "unavailable")
public Payment fetch(String id) { return client.fetch(id); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Which HTTP errors should you retry?
  • What does half-open mean?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 060Interview essentials
# q13

How do sagas and the transactional outbox work?

Say this in the interview

A saga coordinates local transactions across services and uses compensating actions when a later step fails. A transactional outbox writes a business change and an event into the same database transaction, then publishes the event asynchronously.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

The outbox avoids a database-and-broker dual-write gap. Relays can publish more than once, so consumers must be idempotent. Compensation is a business action, not always a literal reversal, and can itself need retries or manual recovery.

Example / implementation sketch
BEGIN;
UPDATE orders SET status = 'CONFIRMED' WHERE id = :id;
INSERT INTO outbox (event_type, payload) VALUES ('OrderConfirmed', :payload);
COMMIT;

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Can an outbox publish duplicates?
  • What if compensation fails?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 061Interview essentials
# q43

What is the difference between orchestration and choreography in a saga?

Say this in the interview

Orchestration uses a coordinator to direct each saga step and its compensation. Choreography lets services react to events without a central workflow controller. Orchestration makes complex workflows easier to follow; choreography reduces central coordination but can make dependencies and failure recovery harder to see.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Both approaches need durable state, idempotent handlers, timeouts and recovery rules. An orchestrator should not become a synchronous single point of failure; persist progress and resume safely. In choreography, maintain clear event ownership and traceability to avoid hidden coupling.

Example / implementation sketch
// Orchestration: coordinator → reserve → charge → confirm
// Choreography: OrderCreated → StockReserved → PaymentCompleted
// Both need explicit failure and compensation paths.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How does a saga resume after a crash?
  • How do you trace an event-driven business transaction?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 062Interview essentials
# q44

How do you evolve an API without breaking existing consumers?

Say this in the interview

Prefer additive changes, preserve existing field meaning and keep old consumers working during rollout. Treat removals, renamed fields and changed semantics as potentially breaking. Use contract tests, consumer visibility and a deprecation period; introduce a new API version when compatibility cannot be maintained.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Even apparently additive changes can break strict clients or exhaustive enum handling. Coordinate database and API changes using expand-and-contract: add compatible structures first, migrate readers and writers, then remove old structures after all users have moved. Monitor old-version traffic before removal.

Example / implementation sketch
// Expand: add optional response field while preserving old fields.
// Migrate: deploy consumers that can use the new representation.
// Contract: remove deprecated fields only after agreed migration.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Can adding an enum value break a consumer?
  • How would you roll out a renamed database column?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 063Interview essentials
# q77

What is a bulkhead and why use it between services?

Say this in the interview

A bulkhead limits the resources one dependency or workload can consume, so its failure does not exhaust the whole service. Use separate concurrency limits or appropriately isolated executors, together with timeouts. A circuit breaker stops calls based on failures; a bulkhead limits how many can run.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Bound both active work and queued work. Giving each dependency a large pool can still exhaust the database, CPU or outbound connections. Measure saturation and reject excess work predictably instead of allowing unbounded waiting. Virtual threads do not remove the need to limit scarce downstream capacity.

Example / implementation sketch
if (!dependencyPermits.tryAcquire()) {
    throw new DependencyBusyException();
}
try { return client.callWithinTimeout(); }
finally { dependencyPermits.release(); }

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How is a bulkhead different from a circuit breaker?
  • Why do virtual threads still need concurrency limits?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 064Interview essentials
# q78

How do you propagate deadlines across a chain of microservices?

Say this in the interview

Set an overall request deadline and give downstream calls only the remaining budget, leaving time for local work and response handling. Use bounded timeouts and stop unnecessary work when cancellation is supported. Independently long timeouts at every hop can exceed the caller’s total latency budget.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Propagate trusted deadline metadata or compute a per-hop budget, accounting for clock skew when using wall-clock timestamps. Include connection setup, retries and queue time in the budget. A timed-out caller does not guarantee downstream processing stopped, so side effects still require idempotency and status recovery.

Example / implementation sketch
Overall budget: 2 seconds
Gateway/local work: reserve 200 ms
Dependency call: at most remaining budget minus response reserve
Retry: allowed only if it fits the same overall deadline

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why should retries share the original deadline?
  • Does a client timeout cancel an external payment?

QUESTION 065Interview essentials
# q79

How do you choose boundaries for microservices?

Say this in the interview

Start with business capabilities, ownership and data invariants rather than splitting every technical layer into a service. Group behavior and data that must change together. Separate services when independent deployment, scaling or team ownership provides enough benefit to justify network calls and distributed consistency.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Frequent synchronous calls and coordinated releases can indicate a boundary is too small or misplaced. Prefer clear APIs and owned data; sharing writable database tables tightly couples services. A modular monolith can preserve boundaries while avoiding distributed-system overhead until the separation is justified.

Example / implementation sketch
Payments: payment lifecycle + provider integration
Ledger: accounting entries + balance invariants
Notifications: delivery preferences + channel workers
// Validate boundaries against real business workflows.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What are signs of a distributed monolith?
  • When is a modular monolith a better starting point?

QUESTION 066Interview essentials
# q141

How do you implement reliable event deduplication?

Say this in the interview

Store a stable event ID with the business change under the same transaction or equivalent atomic mechanism. A uniqueness rule prevents applying the same event twice. A separate check before processing can race under concurrent redelivery.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Deduplication retention must cover the replay horizon. An event ID identifies an occurrence; a business idempotency key may additionally identify a logical operation across different event IDs.

Example / implementation sketch
BEGIN; INSERT INTO processed_events(event_id) VALUES (:id); /* business update */ COMMIT;

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why must the deduplication write be atomic with the effect?
  • What happens after deduplication records expire?

QUESTION 067Interview essentials
# q142

How do you handle poison messages?

Say this in the interview

Identify messages that repeatedly fail because of permanent data or handler problems, stop unbounded retries and route them to a dead-letter or quarantine workflow. Preserve enough diagnostic metadata for investigation without exposing sensitive payloads unnecessarily.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Replay only after correcting the cause and ensuring idempotency. Monitor dead-letter volume and age rather than treating the queue as a place to forget failures.

Example / implementation sketch
Validate → bounded attempts → quarantine → repair → controlled replay

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do you distinguish transient from permanent failures?
  • What makes a replay safe?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 068Interview essentials
# q143

What is the strangler pattern?

Say this in the interview

The strangler pattern replaces an existing system incrementally by routing selected capabilities to new implementations. It reduces the risk of a single large rewrite and allows behavior to be migrated and measured in stages.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Data ownership and synchronization are often harder than routing. Define cutover, rollback and compatibility rules so both implementations do not make conflicting updates.

Example / implementation sketch
Gateway routes migrated /payments operations to new service; remaining routes stay on legacy.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do you move data ownership safely?
  • What enables rollback during migration?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 069Interview essentials
# q144

What is an anti-corruption layer?

Say this in the interview

An anti-corruption layer translates an external or legacy model into your domain’s concepts. It prevents foreign naming, status codes and assumptions from spreading throughout business logic. Keep mapping and error interpretation explicit at the integration boundary.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Translation can hide useful distinctions if oversimplified. Preserve enough context to diagnose external failures and evolve mappings as provider contracts change.

Example / implementation sketch
ProviderStatusAdapter.toDomainStatus(providerResponse.status());

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why avoid using provider DTOs throughout the domain?
  • How would you handle an unknown external status?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 070Interview essentials
# q145

How should services own and share data?

Say this in the interview

A service should control writes to its owned data and expose supported APIs or events for others. Directly sharing writable tables couples deployments and invariants. Replicated read models can support queries when their lag and ownership are explicit.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Cross-service joins and reporting may require separate projections or analytical stores. Avoid assuming that independent tables on the same database eliminate all operational coupling.

Example / implementation sketch
Service A owns account updates; Service B maintains a read projection from account events.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How do you handle cross-service reporting?
  • What risks come from writing another service’s tables?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 071Interview essentials
# q146

How do you design compensation for a failed workflow?

Say this in the interview

Define compensation as an explicit business action that addresses a completed step when later work fails. It may be a refund or release rather than an exact technical rollback. Persist progress and make compensation retryable and idempotent.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Compensation can fail or become impossible after external actions. Track those cases for reconciliation or manual resolution instead of claiming a saga guarantees automatic reversal.

Example / implementation sketch
Reserve stock → charge fails → release reservation; record each transition durably.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What if compensation itself fails?
  • Is a refund equivalent to rolling back a database transaction?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 072Interview essentials
# q147

How do you prevent retry storms?

Say this in the interview

Bound retry attempts, use exponential backoff with jitter and honor relevant retry guidance. Retry only appropriate failures within an overall deadline. Combine admission limits and circuit breakers so an outage does not trigger synchronized repeated traffic.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Retries at multiple layers can multiply attempts. Establish clear ownership of retry policy and use idempotency before retrying operations with side effects.

Example / implementation sketch
Delay = bounded exponential backoff + jitter; stop when deadline or attempt budget is exhausted.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why can retries at three layers multiply load?
  • Which operations need idempotency before retry?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 073Interview essentials
# q148

How do you make an event schema evolve safely?

Say this in the interview

Prefer compatible additions, preserve field meaning and document optionality and defaults. Test real producers and consumers, including strict parsers. Version or migrate intentionally when a change cannot be interpreted safely by existing consumers.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Event history may be replayed long after deployment. Preserve schema identifiers and migration or upcasting rules where required; do not rely only on current live consumers.

Example / implementation sketch
Add optional field → deploy tolerant consumers → publish new producer → monitor compatibility.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Can adding an enum value break consumers?
  • How do replay requirements affect schema evolution?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 074Interview essentials
# q149

What is service discovery?

Say this in the interview

Service discovery maps a logical service name to current reachable instances. It can be supplied by platform DNS, a registry or a routing layer. Clients still need sensible connection management, timeouts and behavior when endpoints change.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Discovery is not a health guarantee for the full operation. Cached DNS, stale connections and readiness propagation can delay endpoint changes.

Example / implementation sketch
Client calls logical name payments.internal rather than a hard-coded pod IP.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why avoid hard-coded pod addresses?
  • Can successful DNS resolution still lead to a failed call?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 075Interview essentials
# q150

How do you design health checks for dependencies?

Say this in the interview

Separate process liveness from readiness to serve useful work. Probe dependency health carefully so a shared outage does not trigger restart loops or remove every instance unnecessarily. Use actual error and latency telemetry alongside synthetic checks.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

A health endpoint may succeed while real traffic fails because of permissions or data-specific behavior. Dependency probes also create load, so bound frequency and timeouts.

Example / implementation sketch
Liveness: internal process; readiness: ability to accept intended traffic; telemetry: actual request outcomes.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Why not put every dependency in liveness?
  • What can a shallow health check miss?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 076Interview essentials
# q151

What is an API composition service?

Say this in the interview

An API composition service gathers data from multiple services into a response suited to a client. It can simplify clients but adds dependency coordination and latency. Define timeouts, partial-result rules and caching based on the endpoint’s requirements.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Fan-out amplifies tail latency and load. Limit concurrency and avoid hiding critical failures behind apparently successful but incomplete responses.

Example / implementation sketch
Customer overview → parallel account and preference reads → bounded aggregation → explicit partial status.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How does fan-out affect p99 latency?
  • When should partial results be allowed?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 077Interview essentials
# q152

What is the backend-for-frontend pattern?

Say this in the interview

A backend for frontend provides an API tailored to a particular client experience, such as mobile or web. It can reduce client round trips and isolate presentation-specific composition while shared business rules remain in domain services.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Multiple BFFs can duplicate logic if responsibilities are unclear. Keep identity propagation and authorization consistent across entry points.

Example / implementation sketch
Mobile BFF returns compact dashboard data; domain services own payment rules.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • How is a BFF different from a generic API gateway?
  • Which logic should remain in domain services?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 078Interview essentials
# q153

How do you handle partial failure in a service call chain?

Say this in the interview

Identify which dependencies are mandatory and which can degrade safely. Apply deadlines and isolation, and return explicit failures or documented partial results. Avoid fabricated fallback values when callers may interpret them as authoritative business data.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

A stale recommendation may be acceptable while a guessed account balance is not. Monitor degraded responses separately so fallback does not hide a prolonged outage.

Example / implementation sketch
Optional recommendation fails → omit with status; required payment authorization fails → return controlled error.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • When is stale data a safe fallback?
  • How do you keep fallback behavior observable?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 079Interview essentials
# q154

How do you distinguish commands from events?

Say this in the interview

A command requests an action from an intended owner and can be rejected. An event records something that happened and may have multiple interested consumers. Naming and ownership should make the difference clear to avoid hidden workflow coupling.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Publishing an event before committing its fact can create false history. Use transactional publication patterns when a database change and event must agree.

Example / implementation sketch
Command: AuthorizePayment; event: PaymentAuthorized.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Can a command fail?
  • Why should an event represent a committed fact?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 080Interview essentials
# q155

What is a correlation ID versus a business operation ID?

Say this in the interview

A correlation ID connects related technical logs or requests. A business operation ID identifies a domain operation such as a transfer across retries and asynchronous steps. Keep both when needed; a new HTTP request should not accidentally create a new logical payment.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Trace IDs may change across workflows or sampling boundaries. Stable business identifiers support reconciliation independently of telemetry retention.

Example / implementation sketch
transfer_id stays stable; request_id and span_id identify individual technical attempts.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Which identifier should survive a payment retry?
  • Why is a trace ID insufficient for long-term reconciliation?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 081Interview essentials
# q156

How do you avoid leaking sensitive data between services?

Say this in the interview

Send only the data needed for the receiving operation, authenticate workloads and enforce authorization. Protect traffic and storage, redact logs and define retention. A private network alone does not justify unrestricted access to customer details.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Copies in queues, traces and caches need the same ownership and retention consideration as primary databases. Use opaque references when full sensitive payloads are unnecessary.

Example / implementation sketch
Event includes customer reference and status, not unnecessary bank credentials or full identity documents.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • Where can sensitive copies accumulate?
  • How do you balance diagnostic detail with data minimization?
Chapter ↑
QUESTION 082Interview essentials
# q157

How do you know when microservices are the wrong choice?

Say this in the interview

Microservices may be the wrong choice when a small team needs tightly coordinated changes, deployment infrastructure is weak or domain boundaries are unclear. A well-structured modular monolith can provide clear ownership with simpler transactions and operations.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Measure independent scaling and deployment benefits against network failures, observability demands and on-call cost. Service count is not a measure of architectural maturity.

Example / implementation sketch
Start with modules and explicit interfaces; separate a module when evidence supports independent operation.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • What evidence justifies extracting a service?
  • What symptoms indicate a distributed monolith?

QUESTION 083Interview essentials
# q14

How would you deploy a Spring Boot service on AWS or Azure?

Say this in the interview

Containerize the service and deploy to ECS/EKS on AWS or Container Apps/AKS on Azure. Use managed identity or workload roles, a managed database, secret storage, health probes and centralized telemetry. Choose the simplest platform that meets operational requirements.

Understand it better · explanation, example & follow-ups

A little deeper

Separate compute scaling from database connection limits. Use multiple availability zones, infrastructure as code, immutable images, least-privilege access and a tested rollback strategy. EKS and AKS add Kubernetes operational overhead.

Example / implementation sketch
// Prefer a workload role / managed identity over static credentials.
// Externalize configuration; expose readiness and liveness endpoints.

Be ready for these follow-ups

  • When would ECS be simpler than EKS?
  • How do you rotate secrets?
